title: Stereoscopic 3D Rendering
prompt:
Use Three.js and the stereoscopic effects in three/addons to implement objects at multiple depths and multiple stereoscopic display modes.

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
Use the following importmap in <head>, and import via ES Modules inside <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { StereoEffect } from 'three/addons/effects/StereoEffect.js';
</script>

[Scene]
(1) The scene must contain at least 5 Mesh objects, arranged from front to back along the Z axis or the camera depth direction, with distinguishable scales/colors.

[Stereoscopic Rendering]
(2) Use StereoEffect (a stereoscopic wrapper based on WebGLRenderer): set eyeSeparation / focal-length-related parameters according to the mode (consult the r170 API and, if necessary, use PerspectiveCamera properties such as focus).

[Controls]
(3) id="eyeSep": range 0.01–0.2, for the interpupillary distance.
(4) id="focalLength": range 10–50, corresponding to StereoEffect or the camera focus (record the user-configured value in the state).
(5) id="stereoMode": <select>, with at least the following options: side-by-side, anaglyph (red-cyan), and cross-eye; when switching modes, change the StereoEffect subclass or use AnaglyphEffect, etc. (import AnaglyphEffect from three/addons/effects if available).

[State Exposure (Required)]
window.__3D_STATE__ = {
  eyeSep: number,
  focalLength: number,
  stereoMode: string,
  objectCount: number,
  fps: number
}

Output a single HTML file that can run when opened directly in a browser.
